prompt: Players describe a VR rhythm game in one word: 'flow'. They slash blocks to music until they lose track of time.
why: Rhythm, motion and music are sensation.
trap: Juice is a technique; the fun is the sensory flow.

prompt: In a racing game, players replay one corner just because the drift feels so good.
trap: They're not trying to beat a time.

prompt: A short game has little story or challenge, but players love its colors, sound and motion.
why: Fun of the senses is sensation.
trap: No role or world is mentioned, just the sensory experience.

prompt: Players say popping the bubbles in a casual game is weirdly satisfying, even without a goal.
tells: weirdly satisfying, even without a goal
why: Pleasure in the feel itself is sensation.
trap: Juice creates it; sensation is the kind of fun.

prompt: Players leave the game running in the background just to hear the music sync with the visuals.
trap: They aren't playing a role; they're enjoying the senses.

prompt: A controller rumble that matches every raindrop makes players say the game feels alive.
why: Physical, sensory feedback as the experience is sensation.
trap: Juice usually means feedback on actions; here the senses are the point.
